acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. PDFree replaces the content under the redaction boxes with a black rectangle at the PDF object level. The original text or image data is not stored elsewhere in the file and cannot be recovered.

name: Does PDFree store or log my files after processing?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. PDFree runs entirely in your browser — there is no backend server that receives your files. Because nothing is uploaded, nothing can be stored, logged, or retained. Your document exists only in your browser's memory for the duration of the session and is cleared when you close the tab.

name: Is PDF redaction done locally or on a server?

acceptedAnswer.text: 100% locally. PDFree processes redaction entirely in your browser — nothing is uploaded to any server.

name: Does redacting a PDF also remove metadata?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Visual redaction does not remove document metadata. Use the Metadata tool on the PDFree homepage separately to remove author names and creation dates.

name: What is the difference between redaction and a black rectangle overlay?

acceptedAnswer.text: Some tools draw a black image on top of text but leave the original text accessible in the PDF's underlying data. PDFree removes the content — a security reviewer who extracts the PDF's text stream would find nothing under the redaction box.

name: Can I redact multiple pages at once?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Navigate between pages using the page buttons and draw boxes on any page. All boxes are applied when you click 'Apply Redaction'.

name: Can I undo a redaction after downloading?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Redaction is a one-way operation — that is what makes it secure. If you need to undo, work from the original unredacted file. Keep the original in a secure location until the redacted version is verified correct.

name: Does PDFree redact text search content too?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. The redaction removes the PDF content stream data for the covered area, including any searchable text within the box bounds.

name: What personal information should I redact before sharing a PDF?

acceptedAnswer.text: Common examples: Social Security numbers, bank account numbers, dates of birth, and signatures. If you're sending a document to a bank, employer, or government office, redacting these first is usually the safest default.
